overview: This 520-page file traces Japan’s wartime foreign exchange resources and controls from 1937 to 1939. State Department analyses estimate gold, overseas balances, and securities available to finance the war in China. Diplomatic correspondence and company records show how exchange permits delayed payments to American cotton exporters, manufacturers, publishers, and shipping lines, while consular reports document currency and trade restrictions in Japanese-controlled areas of China.
interest: Resource estimates sit alongside company balance sheets and diplomatic appeals, revealing how wartime controls shaped individual transactions and U.S. responses.
